items.title: A glacier section collapsed at roughly 5,200 metres on the Nepal-China border, dammed the Lhende Khola above the Bhote Koshi valley and then burst, flooding Nepal's Rasuwa district and Tibet's Gyirong County
items.html: A glacier section collapsed at roughly 5,200 metres on the Nepal-China border, dammed the Lhende Khola above the Bhote Koshi valley and then burst, flooding Nepal's Rasuwa district and Tibet's Gyirong County — the ice-and-rock mass fell about 1,200 metres onto the valley floor. The USGS has formally reclassified its own record (event us7000tbwb): what it first published as a M4.4 earthquake is now titled a M5.2 landslide, with the agency stating that long-period wave analysis and satellite imagery showed the energy came from a glacial collapse and debris flow and that no earthquake occurred. ⚠️ Tolls are provisional and were still climbing through the day — Nepal's Emergency Operations Centre put recovered bodies at 165 and missing at 826 as of Thursday morning (85 security personnel, 466 foreign tourists, 113 domestic tourists, 162 locals), while wire reporting later the same day put the Nepali dead above 350; Xinhua reports 3 dead and 558 missing on the Tibet side, including 260 foreign nationals. This digest does not merge those into a single number, because the government count and the wire count are hours apart and measuring different things. Nepal and China have both since warned that further glacial lakes upstream may burst, and ICIMOD has identified 47 potentially dangerous lakes across the two countries. (USGS event us7000tbwb, Rising Nepal Daily, citing NEOC, Xinhua, Al Jazeera)

items.html: Hezbollah launched two explosive drones at Israeli troops inside the agreed security zone in south Lebanon, and Israel struck Hezbollah weapons infrastructure near Nabatiya in response — the drones went up Wednesday night at the Ali-Taher Ridge; soldiers downed one and lost contact with the second, with no Israeli casualties reported. 2026-08-24.ai: A thin five hours, and the reason is a boundary rather than a quiet field. Most of what this lens would call today's news carries timestamps between 18:05 ET last night and 04:50 ET this morning — the Taiwan indictments, China's cyber-industry plan, and both Hot Chips day-two memory disclosures. All of that sits in digest-day 08-23, which runs to 05:00 ET today, and it is recorded there. Reading only this page would badly understate the last eighteen hours; the 08-23 page is where they are.

At 10:00 ET the three weekday-only outlets this lens depends on — Behavioral Health Business, Fierce Healthcare, MobiHealthNews — had not posted a Monday item at all, so the morning page recorded a gap it could not distinguish from silence and said so.
2026-08-24.global-capital: For four days this lens has carried a characterisation of the Treasury's long-end intervention without knowing what pays for it. Today that gap closed. CNBC's Steve Liesman, citing two senior Treasury officials, reported that the Treasury General Account — the government's operating cash balance at the Fed — is sitting at roughly $935–950bn, some $350–400bn above the $550–600bn level targeted under the previous administration. That cushion is what stands behind the doubled buyback ceiling of up to $4bn per off-the-run issue.
2026-08-24.world-news: Ukraine's 35th Independence Day arrived with both things the map was watching for, and they arrived together. A dated expectation logged on 08-23 said a Coalition of the Willing would meet in Kyiv on the holiday, and separately asked whether Putin's 08-22 warning of something "far more painful and far more destructive" would be acted on around the date. Both resolved today, in the same few hours. The meeting happened — and produced real money, a Norwegian pledge of 85 billion kroner for 2027 and an EU package of €6.1bn. Russia's answer was a nationwide overnight barrage of 2 Oniks missiles, 6 guided air-launched missiles and 143 drones that killed 8 and injured 43, followed by a daylight strike on a residential high-rise in central Chernihiv.
2026-08-24.front: Two things that had been claims for days became facts this morning, and both are about who or what is actually behind a commitment. Then the afternoon delivered a third, and it changed which risk the day was about.

2026-08-25.ai: ⚠️ Afternoon revision: the morning's read of a quiet day did not survive the world-news rebuild. 2026-08-25.mental-health: ⚠️ The afternoon overturned the morning's "quiet day" reading with a single item, and it is a large one: Headspace is being acquired. A public filing revealed that Sword Health — a company that started in digital musculoskeletal care — will absorb Headspace effective 2026-09-14. The most recognisable consumer mental-health brand in the world is becoming a module inside a multi-condition platform sold to employers and payers, which is precisely the pattern The Funding Shift was opened to track, arriving at consumer scale rather than at clinic-rollup scale.
2026-08-25.global-capital: ⚠️ The afternoon added the two facts that make the morning's convergence-on-Nvidia read incomplete. With the mechanically-scored candidate pool back online after eight days, two 08-24 misses surfaced, and they are the same story told from opposite ends. At one end, a price on AI credit: SoftBank's record ¥1tn retail bond now carries a 4.3–4.9% indicative coupon, and Bloomberg reports the reason it is a retail deal at all is that banks were reluctant to take the risk. At the other end, a price on AI's political licence: Texas's attorney general made curbing data centers a US Senate campaign plank and put the state's data-center sales-tax exemption on the block. One is the cost of money for the buildout, the other the cost of permission — and both got marked this week while attention was on an earnings print.
2026-08-25.world-news: Afternoon: the Gaza strike pattern continued rather than tapered, and a second, distinct pressure channel opened on Israel. Four Palestinians were killed, two of them children, per officials — a day after an Israeli airstrike hit the Abu Salim Mosque in Deir al-Balah — and forty members of the US Congress signed a letter urging Israel to release a detained American citizen. That congressional letter is a different mechanism from this morning's Board of Peace criticism: one is the ceasefire's own supervisory body breaking its silence, the other is a domestic US political channel. Both landed within a day of each other, on a war this lens has been logging as low-boil-but-stable.

2026-08-26.ai: Seen across the whole day rather than its first ten hours, 08-26 is the day Nvidia put the circular-financing argument into an SEC filing itself. The earnings beat is the headline — $96.2bn of revenue, data centre up 117%, a Q3 guide of $108bn — but the durable item is the 10-Q filed the same day, which discloses guarantees capped at $105bn tied to an OpenAI affiliate, a further $3.5bn of lease guarantees for AI cloud partners, and a $25bn committed equity pool for AI labs and infrastructure financiers. Until now the scale of Nvidia's exposure to its own customers' buildouts circulated as reported deal value; it is now filed, dated and auditable. Two things sharpen it: the guidance assumes zero China data-centre compute revenue, and receivables concentration widened to five customers holding 72% of the balance. Around that, the day's other movements all point the same direction — AWS committed to two million more Nvidia GPUs, Anthropic leased $45bn of not-yet-shipped silicon, and Salesforce put its CRM inside Claude. Earlier in the day, Zhipu/Z.AI claimed "Ox Alpha," retiring a thread candidate this map had carried unattributed for two runs, and Amazon withdrew a Virginia groundwater application after the state warned the aquifer could not take it.
2026-08-26.mental-health: Two deadlines in this lens passed in silence, and the money kept moving underneath them. Meta did not answer Senator Warner's letter on AI-generated CSAM in its advertisements by the date he set, and neither OpenAI nor Anthropic answered Congress on their rogue-agent incidents — silence is the loud outcome on both, and both are now recorded as such rather than as pending. Against that, the capital side of the lens was not quiet at all: Headspace's sale price surfaced at $200-300 million, roughly a tenth of the $3 billion it was valued at in 2021, turning a deal this map logged yesterday as terms-undisclosed into a near-total write-down of the most recognisable consumer mental-health brand there is. And Onos Health raised $17 million to sell behavioural -health analytics to payers, with CVS Health Ventures on the cap table. ⚠️ Both items broke inside the window this digest originally reported as empty — the coverage critic found them, not the day's own two passes. That correction is the most useful thing in this entry.
2026-08-26.global-capital: Three dated pressures converged on the Fed inside five hours, and none of them resolved. July PCE came in hot on the headline and in line on the core; the White House's deadline for Lisa Cook to answer its removal notice arrived and passed with no public response from her; and Canada's retaliatory tariff schedule — set two weeks out, on 09-08 — put a dated supply-side price shock in front of the September FOMC. The common structure is that each one tightens the Fed's constraint without settling anything: the inflation print argues against the cut the labour data argues for, and the tariff arrives before the meeting rather than after it. One of the three did resolve, in the back half this digest originally could not see: Cook filed. Her attorneys sent a dated written rebuttal to White House Counsel on the deadline day — the formal response the map had spent two runs carefully declining to call either way, correctly. Then Nvidia reported after the close and the day's centre of gravity moved: a beat, a $108bn guide that assumes nothing from China, and — in the 10-Q filed the same day — $105 billion of guarantees to an OpenAI affiliate, a $25 billion equity pool for AI labs, and $500bn+ of third-party capital lined up through Apollo, BlackRock, Blackstone, Brookfield, Goldman and KKR. The circular-financing argument this lens has tracked as an analyst thesis is now an SEC disclosure with a number on it.
2026-08-26.world-news: Hormuz moved for the first time since the deal collapsed — but what moved is an announcement, not an agreement. Iran named a temporary transit corridor through the strait and the Revolutionary Guard said Iran and Oman had "reached agreements" on splitting transit revenue. Oil fell roughly 6% across two days on it. Every official who described the arrangement also disclaimed it: the coordinates are unset, the start date is unset, the revenue mechanics are unset, and Iran's own position is that the strait remains closed until Washington accepts terms. This map has watched two Hormuz arrangements collapse mid-negotiation this year, so the discipline that matters today is refusing to score an announcement as a settlement — the ledger entry stays unresolved, and the reasoning is written into it.
2026-08-26.front: By 15:00 ET, four dated deadlines are sitting in the same honest state: too early to call, not yet silence. The 11:00 ET run reported the White House's Lisa Cook deadline and Meta's Warner deadline as already-passed silence; a closer 15:00 ET check corrected that — Cook's counsel has publicly rebutted the underlying allegations since 08-07, but no formal written response has surfaced, and neither Meta, the Georgia PSC staff decision on Project Camellia, nor tonight's Nvidia earnings (after the 17:00 ET close) have produced evidence either way yet. None of the four should be read as resolved in either direction before the next run — that is itself the finding worth stating plainly, since an earlier framing risked overstating certainty on a same-day deadline. Meanwhile new capital moved on two fronts: Anthropic committed $45 billion over six years to a sixth infrastructure counterparty (Nscale, West Virginia, chips that haven't shipped yet), and SoftBank opened a second bond leg — a $10-20bn wholesale sale alongside its already-priced ¥1 trillion retail bond — with its existing notes selling off the same day. Iran's Hormuz corridor announcement and oil's ~6% two-day drop, and the Ox Alpha resolution, both carry forward unchanged from the morning read below.

2026-08-27.ai: The day after the print, Nvidia spent its capital in two directions at once — buying the open-model ecosystem and courting the Chinese models it is barred from selling into. Reporting escalated overnight from "in talks" to an agreed deal to acquire Hugging Face for about $12.9 billion, which would be its largest acquisition ever, nearly twice Mellanox. On the same day it disclosed it is adding day-zero support and clustering optimisations for DeepSeek and Alibaba Qwen open weights, while its own SEC filing warns that a White House restriction on China-developed models is a business risk. Read together these are one strategy, not two: if the chips cannot go to China, the models can come to the chips, and owning the repository they are distributed through is the same bet made in software. Meanwhile the memory squeeze the earnings call priced in drew a supply response — Kioxia and Sandisk committed over $31 billion to Japanese NAND through 2032 — and 116 companies including every major lab signed a joint letter calling AI-enabled cyber attack an immediate leadership priority.
2026-08-27.mental-health: Two pieces of published work landed today, and between them they frame the same question from opposite ends: what happens when triage stops being a clinical act. An American Prospect investigation reports that one Kaiser Permanente clinic's mental-health triage staffing fell from nine clinicians to three over three years while automated tools took up the routing, with clinicians describing patients left uncontacted or sent to a lower level of care than they needed. On the same day KFF published a state-by-state comparison showing regulators cannot agree on what these tools even are — Illinois and Nevada restricting their use, Utah and Rhode Island regulating disclosure and data instead, with the underlying question of whether an AI mental-health tool is clinical support, a consumer product, or care requiring licensure still open. The Kaiser reporting is what the unresolved question looks like on the ground, three years in. Meanwhile both of this lens's dated deadlines resolved into silence, one of them permanently.
2026-08-27.global-capital: Jackson Hole opened into a market that had already decided the week's question for itself. The symposium began this morning under the theme "Financial Innovation: Implications for Payments and Policy," and the event everyone is positioned for has not happened yet — Kevin Warsh's first keynote as Fed chair is tomorrow at 10:00 ET, three weeks before the September FOMC. What did happen is that Nvidia's beat carried into the cash session and lifted the whole AI complex, so the index level going into a chair's first keynote is being set by one company's guidance rather than by any expectation about rates. Underneath that, the private-capital plumbing kept building: SK Telecom sold nearly half of a new AI data-centre company to KKR and an IMM-led consortium for about $2.2 billion — direct equity in the operating asset, not lending against it, which is the same structure Nvidia's own 10-Q disclosed the night before on a far larger scale. Oil, meanwhile, went back the other way: Brent rebounded more than two dollars after a week that had taken it down over 7% on the Hormuz announcements.
2026-08-27.world-news: The largest story in this lens today is one this map missed for two days, and the way it was missed is worth more than the catch. A glacier collapsed on the Nepal-Tibet border late on 08-25 ET, dammed a river and burst it; the confirmed dead are in the hundreds and the missing are above thirteen hundred across two countries, several hundred of them foreign nationals. Nothing in this map's machinery was ever going to find it. All twelve coverage-critic benchmarks are AI, health-tech or finance publications, so the recall guarantee does not reach a natural disaster by construction; the mechanical world-news pool that might have caught it has been unbuildable for eleven days on an expired credential; and the human-judgment backstop, the flash rail, only fires if the world-news sweep notices first. On 08-25 it did not. A flash is filed today as a late catch, running 24 hours from the catch rather than from the event. Elsewhere: Hezbollah put two drones over Israeli troops in south Lebanon and Israel struck back, and Washington said publicly it is "not talking to Iran" while Qatar's foreign minister flew to Tehran to try to change that.
2026-08-27.front: Two things happened that this map did not find on its own, and both are worth more than the news they carry. The first is that Nvidia's quarterly filing turned the circular-financing argument into a disclosure: guarantees capped at $105 billion tied to an OpenAI affiliate, a $25 billion equity pool for AI labs, $3.5 billion of lease guarantees for cloud partners, and $500 billion-plus of third-party capital lined up through Apollo, BlackRock, Blackstone, Brookfield, Goldman and KKR — a vendor guaranteeing the land and power its customers build on, taking equity in the labs that buy its chips, and routing the funding through private credit. It was filed on 08-26 and read on 08-27. The second is that a glacier collapsed on the Nepal-Tibet border late on 08-25, killed hundreds and left more than thirteen hundred missing across two countries — and no mechanism this map has could have caught it, which is why it took two days. Around those: Nvidia has reportedly agreed to buy Hugging Face for about $12.9 billion while optimising its hardware for the Chinese open models it cannot sell chips into; Jackson Hole opened with Warsh's first keynote as chair still a day away; and at Kaiser Permanente, an investigation reports mental-health triage staffing fell from nine clinicians to three while automated routing took over.

flash.body: A glacier section broke away at roughly 5,200m on the Nepal-China border at 02:52 UTC on 2026-08-26 (22:52 ET, 2026-08-25), fell about 1,200m, dammed the Lhende Khola above the Bhote Koshi valley and then burst, sending a debris flood through Nepal's Rasuwa district and Tibet's Gyirong County; the USGS has formally reclassified the seismic signal it first read as a M4.4 earthquake to a M5.2 landslide, stating no earthquake occurred. Figures are provisional and rising: Nepal's Emergency Operations Centre reported 165 bodies recovered and 826 missing as of Thursday morning, with wire reports since putting the Nepali dead above 350, while Xinhua reports 3 dead and 558 missing on the Tibet side.
